requirements.text: The device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. or, the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
The markings shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2. shall be placed close to the approval mark.
While the approval marking as defined in paragraph 3.3.2. is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown below.
The retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The retroreflective device shall have the approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. clearly legible.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
The retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances the outer surface of retro-reflective devices may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
In normal use there shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector.
The combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The retro-reflecting optical units and filters shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.

When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the retro-reflective device shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1= β2= 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1. shall be used.

For testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

After the tests, the RI (coefficient of luminous intensity) of the retro-reflector shall satisfy the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.; the verification shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.

For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflectors of Red colour shall have minimum RI values in mcd∙lx-1 of 3.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 1.00∙10² at angle of divergence α = 20' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°), 5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = 0°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), 2.8∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±10°, Horizontal β2 = 0°), and 2.5∙10⁰ at angle of divergence α = 1°30' (Vertical β1 = ±5°, Horizontal β2 = ±20°).

Within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°), the RI of the retro-reflector shall not be lower than the values shown in the last two columns of Table 3.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

When testing photometric performances of any retro-reflective device chosen at random, the conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall not be contested if no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.

The retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI, which shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20'.

The retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall have an RI that does not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during the rotation about their axes ±5°, with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20'.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
When the test is completed, the retro-reflective device shall show no visible cracking or appreciable distortion, in particular of its optical component.
The retro-reflecting optical unit shall prevent water from penetrating to the reflecting surface.

The retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The retro-reflective devices shall have the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities, in the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion.
When the test is completed, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device immediately.
The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters of Table A6-1: cycle 1 with a black-standard thermometer (65 ± 3 °C) or cycle 4 with a black-panel thermometer (63 ± 3 °C), exposure periods of 102 min dry and 18 min water spray, irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) or 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm), relative humidity 50 ± 10 %.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.
For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
The lamps shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except that this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
The vehicle shall not emit red light from a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) that is visible from the front of the vehicle.

When there is doubt, the requirement that no red light shall be emitted to the front and no white light shall be emitted to the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; no account is taken of obstacles that were already present when the lamp was type-approved.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5º (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit shall be permitted to be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.

The lamps (devices) shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation when installed on a vehicle, where applicable.

The number of rear retro-reflectors (non-triangular) shall be two, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall have that point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the retro-reflector shall have a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.

The geometric visibility of the retro-reflector shall have a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal; however, where a retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be permitted to have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
